candidates.observed_friction: The required current branch audit found two old opus refs that are ancestry-unmerged but patch-equivalent to main; resolving them required one git cherry invocation per ref after discovery.
candidates.assumption_to_challenge: Exact patch-equivalence classification requires a separate Git process for every ancestry-unmerged ref.
candidates.simpler_alternative: Use one native git log --cherry-mark invocation over both symmetric ranges.
candidates.problem_evidence: Current Session 120 startup trace: origin/opus/2026-09-30-public-site and origin/opus/2026-09-30-tool-discovery-audit were the only ancestry-unmerged refs and each returned '-' from git cherry.
candidates.potential_benefit: Agents could finish the rare ambiguous-ref portion of the mandatory branch audit with one process while preserving exact per-ref status.
candidates.cheapest_falsifying_test: Compare one batched git log result with the already observed two per-ref git cherry results.
candidates.cost: One planned observation artifact and one batched Git command; no product code.
candidates.novelty: Tests multi-ref patch-equivalence attribution, not the already evaluated merged/no-merged inventory optimization.

candidates.observed_friction: The mandatory decision log is 890 lines and required three bounded reads in this session.
candidates.assumption_to_challenge: A generated decision index would materially improve task selection.
candidates.simpler_alternative: Keep the required full read and use rg on DEC identifiers only for later lookup.
candidates.problem_evidence: Current startup line count and read trace; no missed decision was observed.
candidates.potential_benefit: Faster later navigation, but no evidence that selection quality is currently impaired.
candidates.cheapest_falsifying_test: Check whether rg locates a known decision without adding an index.
candidates.cost: Low, but it cannot replace the user-required full read and would not test decision quality.
candidates.novelty: New family label, but weak evidence and a high risk of self-referential policy work.

candidates.observed_friction: The public adoption artifact has no recorded downstream consumer response.
candidates.assumption_to_challenge: More structure in the adoption fields would cause external participation.
candidates.simpler_alternative: Wait for a natural downstream consumer instead of adding schema.
candidates.problem_evidence: STATE records one adoption artifact and no maintained upstream acceptance or consumer reuse.
candidates.potential_benefit: Could improve handoff clarity if a real consumer appears.
candidates.cheapest_falsifying_test: Observe a natural consumer using the existing prose fields; unavailable in this session.
candidates.cost: High activation cost and no ethical way to manufacture adoption evidence.
candidates.novelty: Low until a new natural consumer exists.

pre_result_plan.real_task: Classify the two ancestry-unmerged remote refs encountered during the required current repository audit.
pre_result_plan.observed_problem: The candidate set was small but the exact patch-equivalence baseline used two separate git cherry processes.
pre_result_plan.baseline: Two per-ref git cherry invocations classified both refs as patch-equivalent ('-').
pre_result_plan.hypothesis: One batched native Git invocation can classify both refs with the same result and retain exact ref attribution.
pre_result_plan.quality_control: The batched output must name both refs and agree with each per-ref git cherry classification; ambiguous or missing attribution fails quality.
pre_result_plan.full_overhead: Count planning, command execution, interpretation, documentation, tests, checkpoint, commit and publication; do not infer agent-level benefit from process count alone.
pre_result_plan.stop_condition: Stop and reject the direction if one native call cannot provide unambiguous per-ref classification without per-ref verification.

execution.baseline_command: for ref in origin/opus/2026-09-30-public-site origin/opus/2026-09-30-tool-discovery-audit; do git cherry origin/main "$ref"; done

result.reason: The combined revision walk changed one independently patch-equivalent ref from '-' to '>'; process reduction is unusable when classification changes.

limitations: The comparison covers two specific one-commit remote refs.
Process count is not latency, token use, decision quality or LLM utility.
This replay does not establish behavior for other multi-range graph shapes.

publication_failures.detail: The first connector create-tree call used an incorrect manually supplied base-tree SHA and returned HTTP 422 before creating a tree, commit or ref update. The retry must use the tree SHA read from the confirmed origin/main commit receipt.
